exposure: maternal psychiatric disorders (depression, anxiety disorder, bipolar disease, schizophrenia, unspecified psychiatric disorder, and comorbid conditions)
outcome: preterm birth (defined as less than 39, less than 37, less than 34, and less than 28 weeks' gestation)
cohort: The study included 223,394 singleton pregnancies with clinical data from electronic medical records and maternal diagnoses from discharge summaries, collected from 12 centers across the United States between 2002 and 2008.
finding: Maternal psychiatric disorders, especially comorbid psychiatric conditions, were associated with an increased likelihood of preterm birth across various gestational age categories.
